DASH.name: DASH Diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension)
DASH.medical_background: The DASH diet is a clinically-proven dietary pattern designed to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiovascular disease risk. It emphasizes whole grains, lean proteins, fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy while limiting sodium, saturated fats, and added sugars.

daily_servings.sweets: limited to 5 or fewer per week

MEDITERRANEAN.name: Mediterranean Diet
MEDITERRANEAN.medical_background: The Mediterranean diet emphasizes heart-healthy monounsaturated fats from olive oil, fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids, whole grains, legumes, vegetables, and moderate wine consumption. This pattern has been associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality and better metabolic control.

LOW_GLYCEMIC.name: Low Glycemic Index Diet
LOW_GLYCEMIC.medical_background: The Low Glycemic Index diet focuses on carbohydrates that are slowly absorbed, promoting stable blood glucose levels and reducing insulin spikes. This pattern is particularly beneficial for patients with impaired glucose metabolism.

RENAL_FRIENDLY.name: Renal-Friendly Diet
RENAL_FRIENDLY.medical_background: The Renal-Friendly diet is designed to reduce the workload on compromised kidneys by controlling sodium, potassium, phosphorus, and protein intake. This helps slow kidney disease progression and manage electrolyte balance.

CELIAC_FRIENDLY.name: Gluten-Free Diet
CELIAC_FRIENDLY.medical_background: The Gluten-Free diet eliminates all sources of gluten (found in wheat, barley, rye) to allow intestinal healing in individuals with celiac disease. This diet prevents autoimmune intestinal damage and allows nutrient absorption.
